q: Which French forward did Manchester United sign from Leeds United in November 1992?
sub: A million pounds, and four league titles at Old Trafford.
note: Confirmed on his own article: left Leeds for Manchester United for 1 million pounds on 26 November 1992, four league titles in five years at United. Not a duplicate of the shipping Cantona row, which is about the 1995 kick at Crystal Palace.

q: Which Dutch forward did Arsenal sign from Inter Milan in 1995?
sub: He won both the PFA and FWA player of the year awards in 1998.
note: Inter 1993 to 1995 then Arsenal confirmed. His article: named FWA Footballer of the Year and PFA Players' Player of the Year in April and May 1998.

q: Which Italian forward did Chelsea sign from Parma in November 1996?
sub: Chelsea fans voted him their best ever player in 2003.
note: Confirmed: joined Chelsea from Parma in November 1996, and voted best ever Chelsea player by the fans in early 2003.

q: Which German striker did Tottenham Hotspur sign from Monaco in 1994?
sub: He stayed one season and left for Bayern Munich.
note: Confirmed: signed from Monaco in July 1994 for 2 million pounds, one season (1994-95), then Bayern Munich 1995-97. First spell only, so no clash with the loan row.

q: Which Norwegian striker did Manchester United sign from Molde in 1996?
sub: He scored six minutes into his debut against Blackburn Rovers.
note: Confirmed: joined United from Molde on 29 July 1996 for 1.5 million pounds, and scored six minutes into his substitute debut against Blackburn on 25 August 1996.

q: Which Czech goalkeeper did Chelsea sign from Rennes in 2004?
sub: He kept twenty-four clean sheets in his first season.
note: Confirmed: Rennes agreed his move to Chelsea for 7 million pounds, joined 2004, and won the 2004-05 Golden Glove with a record 24 league clean sheets.

q: Which Dutch defender did Liverpool sign from Southampton in January 2018?
sub: The 75 million pound fee was a world record for a defender at the time.
note: Confirmed, and the record claim is anchored to the time so it has no shelf-life problem. Different leg of his career from the Celtic row, so not a mirror.

q: Which Senegalese forward did Liverpool sign from Southampton in 2016?
sub: The most expensive African player in the world at the time.
note: Confirmed: 34 million pounds in 2016, most expensive African player in history at that time. Different transfer from the Salzburg row, so not a mirror.

q: Which French midfielder did Arsenal sign from AC Milan in 1996 and later make club captain?
sub: He took the armband after Tony Adams retired in 2002.
note: Question confirmed (AC Milan to Arsenal 1996 for 3.5 million pounds, captain from 2002). Sub said he took the armband from Adams in May 2002; his article says Adams' retirement in May 2002 meant Vieira became club captain, i.e. for 2002-03, so I removed the implied May handover.

q: Which Frenchman won the Premier League with Leicester City in 2015-16 and with Chelsea in 2016-17?
note: Confirmed on his article: first outfield player to win consecutive English titles with different clubs since Cantona. Easy tier is right, this is a famous double.

q: Which Algerian winger was named PFA Players' Player of the Year in 2016 while at Leicester City?
sub: The first African player to win the award.
note: Confirmed: won the award on 25 April 2016, and his own article states he was the first African to earn the accolade, so the first-player claim survives the article test.

q: Which Belgian defender captained Manchester City to the Premier League title in 2011-12?
sub: He won four league titles at City and left in 2019.
note: Confirmed: given the captaincy in 2011-12 and led City to the title. Honours list shows exactly four Premier League titles (2011-12, 2013-14, 2017-18, 2018-19) and he left in 2019.

q: Which Serbian defender did Manchester United sign from Spartak Moscow, joining in January 2006?
sub: Five league titles, and the captaincy from 2010.
note: Confirmed: moved from Spartak Moscow to United in January 2006, won five Premier League titles, appointed club captain in 2010.

q: Which Brazilian playmaker did Middlesbrough sign from Sao Paulo in 1995?
sub: He had three separate spells on Teesside.
note: Confirmed: signed from Sao Paulo in October 1995 for 4.75 million pounds, and his article says he had three spells at Middlesbrough.

q: Which South Korean did Manchester United sign from PSV Eindhoven in 2005?
sub: The first Asian player to become a Premier League champion.
note: Confirmed: 4 million pounds from PSV in July 2005. The first-Asian claim is stated on his own article in those exact terms for the 2006-07 title, so it passes the article test.

q: Which French winger did Newcastle United sign from Paris Saint-Germain in 1995?
sub: Tottenham Hotspur signed him in July 1997, along with Les Ferdinand.
note: Question confirmed (PSG to Newcastle, July 1995). The sub claimed the Tottenham move was for the same fee: his own article says 2.5 million pounds both times but the 1997-98 Tottenham season article says 2 million, so I replaced the fee claim with the Ferdinand detail that both sources carry.

q: Which Italian striker did Middlesbrough sign from Juventus in 1996?
sub: Sixteen league goals, and Middlesbrough still went down.
note: Confirmed: 7 million pounds from Juventus in 1996, 16 league goals in 33 games in 1996-97, Middlesbrough relegated that season.

q: Which Colombian forward did Newcastle United sign from Parma in February 1996?
sub: He was sold back to Parma two years later.
note: Confirmed: 6.7 million pounds in February 1996, and sold back to Parma for 6 million at the end of January 1998, two years later.

q: Which Dutch defender did Manchester United sign from PSV Eindhoven in 1998 for 10.6 million pounds?
sub: The most expensive defender in the world at the time.
note: Confirmed word for word: April 1998, 10.6 million pounds, then the most expensive defender in history.

q: Which Dutch winger did Arsenal sign from Ajax in 1997?
sub: He left for Barcelona in 2000 for 25 million pounds.
note: Confirmed: Ajax to Arsenal in 1997, and a 25 million pound move to Barcelona in 2000.

q: Which club did Arsenal sign Nwankwo Kanu from in February 1999?
sub: He had come through heart surgery in 1996 while at Inter.
note: Confirmed: signed by Arsenal in February 1999 after twelve league games for Inter, and Inter paid for his aortic valve operation in late 1996.

q: Which French goalkeeper did Manchester United sign from Monaco in 2000 to replace Peter Schmeichel?
sub: He won two league titles before being loaned back to Marseille.
note: Confirmed: 7.8 million pounds from Monaco in 2000, signed because Ferguson wanted a replacement for the departed Schmeichel. Won 2000-01 and 2002-03, then loaned to Marseille in January 2004.

q: Which Dutch goalkeeper did Fulham sign from Juventus in 2001?
sub: Manchester United took him from Fulham four years later.
note: Confirmed: joined Fulham from Juventus on 1 August 2001 for 7 million pounds, and moved to Manchester United in 2005.

q: Which Croatian midfielder did Tottenham Hotspur sign from Dinamo Zagreb in 2008?
sub: Tottenham turned down a 40 million pound Chelsea bid for him in 2011.
note: Both halves confirmed. Chelsea's 2011 bids went 22 million, then 27 million, and on deadline day 40 million, all rejected, so the sub's figure is the right one of the three.

q: Which club did Southampton sign Virgil van Dijk from in 2015?
sub: Thirteen million pounds, on a five-year contract.
note: Confirmed: 1 September 2015, five-year contract, reported 13 million pounds, from Celtic.

q: Which club did Southampton sign Sadio Mane from in 2014?
note: Confirmed: 1 September 2014, 11.8 million pounds from Red Bull Salzburg, a Southampton club record at the time.

q: Which Argentine striker did West Ham United sign from Corinthians in August 2006?
sub: The third-party ownership deal cost West Ham a 5.5 million pound fine.
note: Confirmed: announced 31 August 2006 from Corinthians, and in April 2007 West Ham were fined a record 5.5 million pounds over the Tevez and Mascherano signings.

q: Which club did Manchester City sign Robinho from in 2008 for 32.5 million pounds?
sub: He top scored for City in his first season with fourteen goals.
note: Confirmed: 1 September 2008, 32.5 million pounds from Real Madrid. Watch out that his article also says 14 goals in his first Real Madrid season, but the City line is separately sourced: top scorer in 2008-09 with 14 league goals.

q: Which Frenchman did Manchester United sign from Monaco in January 2006, going on to win five league titles?
sub: He finished his career with a spell at West Ham United in 2018.
note: Facts all confirmed (January 2006 from Monaco, five Premier League titles listed in his honours, West Ham from February 2018 as his last club). Only reworded the clumsy and who went on to construction so it reads aloud cleanly.

q: Which Nigerian striker did West Bromwich Albion sign from Lokomotiv Moscow in 2010?
sub: Fifteen league goals in his first season made him their top scorer.
note: Confirmed: signed 20 August 2010 from Lokomotiv Moscow, and ended 2010-11 as West Brom's top scorer with 15 league goals in 32 games.

q: Which club did Leicester City sign N'Golo Kante from in 2015?
sub: Reported at about 5.6 million pounds in August 2015.
note: Confirmed: joined Leicester from Caen on 3 August 2015, fee reported as 8 million euros or about 5.6 million pounds.

q: Which Spaniard did Swansea City sign from Rayo Vallecano in 2012 for two million pounds?
sub: He scored eighteen league goals in his first season.
note: Confirmed: 20 July 2012, 2 million pounds from Rayo Vallecano, and 18 goals in 35 league games in 2012-13 (22 in all competitions, so the league figure is the right one to quote).

q: Which Dutchman became Chelsea player-manager in 1996 when Glenn Hoddle left to manage England?
sub: He won the FA Cup in 1997, Chelsea's first major trophy in 26 years.
note: Confirmed: appointed player-manager in 1996 a year after joining under Hoddle, and his article calls the 1997 FA Cup the club's first major title for 26 years.

q: Which Italian replaced Ruud Gullit as Chelsea player-manager in February 1998?
sub: The first Italian to manage in the Premier League.
note: Confirmed: appointed on 12 February 1998 after Gullit's sacking, and his own article says he became the first Italian to manage in the Premier League.

q: Which Ghanaian striker joined Leeds United from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 1995?
sub: A loan first, then 3.4 million pounds to make it permanent.
note: Confirmed and correctly framed: January 1995, initially on loan with an option to sign permanently for 3.4 million pounds. This is the one loan-then-buy row that already had it right.

q: Which Nigerian midfielder joined Bolton Wanderers on a free transfer from Paris Saint-Germain in 2002?
sub: He captained them to the 2004 League Cup final.
note: Confirmed: joined Bolton on 18 June 2002 on a free after leaving PSG, and as captain led them to the 2004 League Cup final, lost to Middlesbrough.

q: Which club did Gianfranco Zola join when he left Chelsea in 2003?
sub: Seven seasons at Stamford Bridge, then home to Sardinia.
note: Confirmed: left in the summer of 2003 for Cagliari, from his native Sardinia, after seven seasons from November 1996 to 2002-03.

q: Which Ukrainian did Chelsea sign from AC Milan in 2006 for 30.8 million pounds?
sub: A record fee for an English club at the time, for nine league goals.
note: Confirmed: 28 May 2006, 30.8 million pounds, a record for a player signed by an English club, and his Chelsea league return was 9 goals in 48 games.

q: Which Argentine did Manchester United sign from Lazio in 2001 for 28.1 million pounds?
sub: The most expensive transfer in English football at the time.
note: Confirmed: 12 July 2001, 28.1 million pounds from Lazio, the most expensive transfer in English football at that time.

q: Which Bulgarian did Tottenham Hotspur sign from Bayer Leverkusen in 2006?
sub: The most expensive Bulgarian footballer at the time.
note: Confirmed: agreed with Leverkusen in May 2006, joined in July, and the fee made him the most expensive Bulgarian footballer ever. The shipping deck only has his 2008 move to United, so this is a different fact.

q: Which French club did Leeds United take Eric Cantona on loan from in January 1992?
sub: A hundred thousand pounds for the loan, then 900,000 to buy him.
note: Confirmed exactly: arrival announced January 1992, 100,000 pounds to Nimes for a loan until 15 April, then another 900,000 to sign him permanently.

q: Which Italian club did Jurgen Klinsmann rejoin Tottenham Hotspur from in December 1997?
sub: Nine goals in fifteen league games, and Tottenham beat the drop.
note: The club and the season are right, but the sources disagree on the deal: his own article calls it a loan from Sampdoria, while the 1997-98 Tottenham season article lists him as a free transfer on 28 December 1997. Reworded to rejoin from so the row does not rest on the disputed word, and replaced the loose kept Tottenham up sub with the sourced 9 goals in 15 league games plus the club article's beat the drop.

q: Jurgen Klinsmann scored four goals in a 6-2 away win for Tottenham Hotspur in 1998. Against which club?
note: Fact confirmed to the date: Wimbledon away, 2 May 1998, 6-2, Klinsmann four. Only the src changed, because his own article does not mention the game at all; swapped it for the club season article, whose results table carries it.

q: Juninho returned to Middlesbrough on loan in 1999-2000. Which Spanish club was he on loan from?
sub: Four goals in 24 games, then straight back to Madrid.
note: Confirmed: loaned back to Middlesbrough for 1999-2000 from Atletico Madrid, four goals in 24 games, then returned to Atletico. Second spell, correctly separated from the 1995 signing row.

q: Which English club did Fabrizio Ravanelli join on a free transfer in 2001, four years after leaving Middlesbrough?
sub: They went down in 2002 and later deferred his wages.
note: Confirmed: joined Derby in July 2001 on a free on a two-year deal, four years after leaving Middlesbrough for Marseille in 1997. Derby were relegated in 2002 and deferred his wage payments.

q: Which club did Faustino Asprilla score a Champions League hat-trick against for Newcastle United in 1997?
sub: A 3-2 win at St James' Park on 17 September 1997.
note: Confirmed: 17 September 1997, hat-trick in a 3-2 win over Barcelona. Venue checked separately on the 1997-98 Newcastle season article, which gives St James' Park.

q: Which West Ham United signing of 1995 was wrongly reported by a tabloid to be living in a caravan?
sub: Gone by car again was misheard as gone to his caravan, and the Sun ran it.
note: The story checks out, and his article has a Caravan myth section: his agent said he has probably gone by car again, a Clubcall reporter heard gone to his caravan, and the Sun ran Barmy Boogers Living in a Caravan. Only rewrote the sub, which was garbled to the point of being unreadable aloud.

q: Which Manchester United goalkeeper let a weak Matt Le Tissier shot slip through his legs in September 1999?
sub: One paper christened him the Blind Venetian. He played four league games.
note: Confirmed: 25 September 1999 against Southampton, and four league appearances in total. Changed the papers to one paper, because his article credits the Blind Venetian nickname to a single newspaper. He had come from Venezia, which is where the gag comes from.

q: Which Italian club did Manchester United sell Jaap Stam to in 2001?
sub: His book Head to Head had just upset Sir Alex Ferguson.
note: Confirmed: sold to Lazio early in the 2001-02 season after Ferguson was reportedly upset by the allegations in his autobiography Head to Head.

q: Which Arsenal forward scored three times in fifteen minutes at Chelsea in October 1999 to turn 2-0 down into a 3-2 win?
note: Confirmed on both sides: his article says a hat-trick in fifteen minutes against Chelsea in October 1999 from 2-0 down, and the 1999-2000 Chelsea season article has it at Stamford Bridge, Flo 38 and Petrescu 52 against Kanu 75, 83, 90.

q: Petr Cech fractured his skull in October 2006 in a collision at which club's ground?
sub: Stephen Hunt's knee caught his head inside the first minute.
note: Confirmed: Madejski Stadium, 14 October 2006, Stephen Hunt's right knee hit his head inside the first minute, depressed skull fracture.

q: Patrice Evra was taken off at half-time on his Manchester United debut in January 2006. Against which club?
sub: United lost 3-1. Ferguson called it a bit of a gamble.
note: Confirmed: debut 14 January 2006, 3-1 away defeat to Manchester City, substituted at half-time, and Ferguson said maybe it was a bit of a gamble playing Evra.

q: Which Ivorian defender did Arsenal sign from ASEC Mimosas in 2002 for 150,000 pounds?
sub: He was a regular centre-back in the unbeaten 2003-04 season.
note: Confirmed: signed from ASEC Mimosas on 14 February 2002 for 150,000 pounds after a trial, and Wenger paired him with Sol Campbell from the start of the unbeaten season.

q: Which Brazilian midfielder did Arsenal sign from Atletico Mineiro in 2002, nicknamed the invisible wall?
sub: He played 32 of the 38 games in the unbeaten season.
note: Confirmed: 4.5 million pounds from Atletico Mineiro in July 2002, often called the invisible wall, and his article says he played 32 of Arsenal's 38 unbeaten league games.

q: Which American club did Thierry Henry rejoin Arsenal on loan from in January 2012?
sub: He wore number 12 because Theo Walcott had 14.
note: Confirmed: re-signed on a two-month loan on 6 January 2012 from New York Red Bulls, and took number 12 because Walcott had inherited his 14.

q: Thierry Henry's 2012 loan at Arsenal ended with a stoppage-time league winner against which club?
sub: He had marked his return with the only goal against Leeds in the FA Cup.
note: Confirmed: his last league game on loan brought a stoppage-time winner in a 2-1 win over Sunderland, and his second debut was the only goal against Leeds in the FA Cup third round.

q: Which club did Papiss Cisse score the BBC Goal of the Season against in May 2012?
sub: Curled in from 37 yards with the outside of his foot, over Petr Cech.
note: Confirmed down to the detail: 2 May 2012 at Stamford Bridge, curled with the outside of his foot from 37 yards, looped over Cech, chosen as the BBC's Goal of the Season.

q: Which Georgian did Manchester City sign from Dinamo Tbilisi in 1995?
sub: He later played for Derby County after a short spell at Ajax.
note: Confirmed: joined City from Dinamo Tbilisi in 1995 for a reported 2 million pounds, left for Ajax in 1998 after a second relegation, made 12 league appearances there, then Derby County.

q: Which Costa Rican scored for Derby County at Old Trafford in April 1997, beating four Manchester United players?
sub: Derby won 3-2 and their fans later voted it the club's best goal.
note: Confirmed: 5 April 1997, on his Derby debut, beat four United players before slotting past Schmeichel in a 3-2 win, later voted the greatest goal in the club's history by Derby fans.

q: Which Dane became the first goalkeeper to score a Premier League goal, playing for Aston Villa in October 2001?
sub: It came in a 3-2 defeat at Everton. He finished his career at Manchester City.
note: Confirmed on his own article: on 20 October 2001 he became the first goalkeeper to score a Premier League goal, in a 3-2 defeat away to Everton, and Manchester City in 2002-03 was his last club.

q: Which Spaniard did Arsenal sign from Barcelona in 2003 and make club captain five years later?
sub: He was 16, and became Arsenal's youngest first-team player.
note: Confirmed: came from Barcelona's academy in 2003, youngest ever Arsenal first-team player at 16 years and 177 days, named club captain on 24 November 2008, five years later.

q: Which South African defender did Leeds United sign from Kaizer Chiefs in 1994?
sub: Nelson Mandela called him his hero. They nicknamed him the Chief.
note: Dropped the fee from the question: his article says the 250,000 pounds bought Radebe and Phil Masinga together, so attaching it to Radebe alone is wrong. The answer stays unique because Masinga was a striker. Also trimmed the sub, since the article credits the Chief nickname to his spells at both clubs rather than to Leeds fans.

q: Which Newcastle United winger played the trumpet and formed a salsa band called the Geordie Latinos?
sub: The first Peruvian to play in the Premier League.
note: Both confirmed on his own article: noted for his trumpet playing and his salsa band The Geordie Latinos, and the first Peruvian to play in the Premier League.

q: Which Trinidad and Tobago striker did Manchester United sign from Aston Villa in 1998 for 12.6 million pounds?
sub: He shared the Golden Boot that season on eighteen goals.
note: Transfer confirmed: 20 August 1998, 12.6 million pounds from Villa. The sub said he top scored in 1998-99, but the Golden Boot was shared three ways with Hasselbaink and Owen on 18 each, and the shipping deck already answers that season's top scorer as Hasselbaink, so the old sub contradicted a live question.

q: Which Colombian striker spent the 2014-15 season on loan at Manchester United from Monaco?
sub: He scored four times and United did not take up the option to buy.
note: Confirmed: season-long loan for 6 million pounds with an option at 43 million, and on 24 May 2015 United announced they would not exercise it after 4 goals in 29 appearances.

q: Chelsea fielded the first Premier League starting eleven with no English player in it on Boxing Day 1999. Against which club?
sub: Gianluca Vialli's side won 2-1 at The Dell.
note: Confirmed: 26 December 1999, away win over Southampton, described as the first team in Football League history to field a starting eleven without an English player, so the Premier League framing is safe. The season article's fixture list gives The Dell, and Vialli was manager.

q: Arsene Wenger named an Arsenal squad with no British player in it for the first time in February 2005. Which club were they playing?
sub: 14 February 2005. Paul Merson called it a joke.
note: Confirmed: 14 February 2005 against Crystal Palace, a squad with no British player, a first in the club's history, and Merson called it a joke. Arsenal won 5-1.

q: Which French World Cup winning captain spent 1999-2000 at Chelsea and won the FA Cup there?
sub: One season, from Juventus, then Valencia and retirement.
note: Confirmed: Juventus to Chelsea for 1999-2000, won the 1999-2000 FA Cup, then Valencia and retirement after the 2001 Champions League final.

q: Which Dane made seven Premier League appearances for Chelsea in 1998-99 after arriving from Rangers?
sub: He was unhappy from the start and left for FC Copenhagen.
note: Confirmed: Rangers 1994-98 then Chelsea, and the stats table gives exactly 7 Premier League appearances in 1998-99 before he moved to Copenhagen, having been openly unhappy in London.

q: Which Romanian did Tottenham Hotspur sign from PSV Eindhoven in September 1994 and sell to Barcelona a year later?
sub: Twenty-three league games and three goals in his only season.
note: Confirmed: joined from PSV on 9 September 1994, left for Barcelona for 3 million pounds after less than a year, and his 1994-95 line is 23 league games and 3 goals.

q: Which Romanian joined Tottenham Hotspur from Steaua Bucharest in 1994 and later lost his West Ham contract over a work permit?
sub: He left England for Club America in 1996.
note: Confirmed but reworded. His article says he was sold to West Ham, played ten games, then hit work permit problems and had his contract broken, so lost a West Ham deal wrongly suggested the move itself collapsed. Steaua to Tottenham in 1994 and Club America in the summer of 1996 both check out.

q: Which French World Cup winner spent the 2000-01 season at Middlesbrough after leaving Real Madrid?
sub: He joined Olympiacos the following summer.
note: Confirmed by his club timeline: Real Madrid 1997-2000, Middlesbrough 2000-01, Olympiacos from 2001. No other French World Cup winner fits, so the answer stays unique.

q: Which former Real Madrid defender joined Bolton Wanderers from Al-Rayyan in 2004 and retired a season later?
sub: Steve McManaman had recommended the move to him.
note: Confirmed: Al-Rayyan 2003-04, Bolton 2004-05, retirement announced 10 May 2005, on the advice of his former Real Madrid teammate Steve McManaman. The Al-Rayyan clause is what keeps Ivan Campo, also an ex-Madrid defender at Bolton, out of the answer.

q: Which Japanese midfielder spent 2005-06 on loan at Bolton Wanderers from Fiorentina?
sub: He retired at the age of 29 when that season ended.
note: Confirmed: moved to Bolton on loan in August 2005 from Fiorentina, his last season as a professional, and he announced his retirement on 3 July 2006 aged 29.

q: Which Italian defender was sent off three times in a single season at Everton before going back to Perugia?
sub: Three reds in 27 games in 1998-99.
note: Confirmed word for word: sent off three times in just 27 games in 1998-99 at Everton, then returned to Perugia in 1999. This is his second Perugia spell, correctly described as going back.

q: Which Croatian striker cost Aston Villa 5.8 million pounds in 2001 and never scored for them?
sub: Nine appearances in two and a half years, seven off the bench, and no goals.
note: The fee and the flop are confirmed (5.8 million pounds, 20,000 a week, nine appearances in two and a half years with seven as a substitute, zero goals). Took out never starting a league game: his own article does not say it and its own numbers imply a start or two, while the stats table gives him 8 league appearances. Zero goals for Villa is in both the table and the prose.

q: Which Ukrainian did Tottenham Hotspur sign from Dynamo Kyiv in 2000 for 11 million pounds?
sub: He later had two loan spells at Fenerbahce.
note: Confirmed: sold to Tottenham on 17 May 2000 for 11 million pounds, a club record, and his article says he spent two consecutive loan spells at Fenerbahce.

q: Which German full-back scored the 15,000th goal in Premier League history, for Fulham against Chelsea in December 2006?
sub: The goal earned him the nickname 15,000 Volz. He cycled to home games.
note: Confirmed: 30 December 2006, the 15,000th Premier League goal, for Fulham against Chelsea, and he is listed as a right-back. Swapped the unsourced cult hero line for the nickname 15,000 Volz, which his article does carry, and kept the bicycle.

q: Which Finn scored seventeen Premier League goals on loan at Birmingham City from Chelsea in 2003-04?
sub: Birmingham bought him outright in 2005 for 3.5 million pounds.
note: Confirmed: 17 Premier League goals for Birmingham in 2003-04 while a Chelsea player, more league goals than any other Chelsea player that season, and he signed permanently in the summer of 2005 for 3.5 million pounds.

q: Which Frenchman scored five goals in four games on loan at Birmingham City in 2003 and helped keep them up?
sub: He signed permanently that May and managed one more goal.
note: Confirmed: a run of 5 goals in 4 matches took Birmingham out of the relegation zone to 13th, he signed a permanent two-year deal in May 2003, and then scored once in 15 appearances.

q: Which Portuguese forward did Manchester United sign from Vitoria de Guimaraes in 2010 having never been watched by Sir Alex Ferguson?
sub: Carlos Queiroz recommended him. He played seven times.
note: Now fully confirmed, so the likely can be upgraded: United agreed a fee on 11 August 2010 five weeks after he joined Guimaraes, Ferguson admitted he had never seen him play and only met him the day before, Queiroz recommended him, and his stats give exactly seven United appearances, all in 2010-11.

q: Which Swede acted as Attilio Lombardo's interpreter when the pair took caretaker charge of Crystal Palace in 1998?
sub: Palace went down anyway. Brolin retired that August.
note: Confirmed on both articles: Lombardo, along with Brolin as an interpreter, was appointed caretaker player-manager for the rest of the season; Palace were relegated and Brolin announced his retirement on 12 August 1998. Worth knowing the Palace chairman insisted Brolin was merely the interpreter, not an assistant coach.

q: Which Portuguese forward refused to play for West Ham United in 1996 until he was given squad number ten?
sub: He had arrived from AC Milan and played nine games.
note: Confirmed: his article says he infamously refused to play until he was given squad number 10, he came from AC Milan where he played once in 1995-96, and his West Ham line is nine games.

q: Which Manchester City defender became the first East Asian to score in the Premier League, in October 2002?
sub: He and Fan Zhiyi were the first Chinese players in English league football, at Crystal Palace in 1998.
note: Both firsts are on his own article: first East Asian footballer to score in the Premier League, for City in 2002 with a BBC report dated 26 October, and he and Fan Zhiyi became the first Chinese footballers to play in the English leagues after signing for Crystal Palace in August 1998.

q: Which Latvian did Southampton sign from Skonto in 1999, the first from his country to play in the Premier League?
sub: They called him the Latvian Michael Owen.
note: The first-player claim is on his own article in those words: joined Southampton from Skonto in March 1999 for about 800,000 pounds after work permit trouble, becoming the first Latvian to play in the Premier League. Also dubbed the Latvian Michael Owen. The article now sits at Marians Pahars, which matches the answer spelling.

q: Which Senegalese forward came on for Southampton in 1996 after a caller posing as George Weah said he was his cousin?
sub: Matt Le Tissier said he ran about like Bambi on ice. He lasted 14 days.
note: Confirmed: November 1996, the caller claiming to be Weah told Souness that Dia was his cousin, Le Tissier said he ran around the pitch like Bambi on ice, and he was released 14 days into his contract.

q: Which Nigerian striker brought himself on as a substitute in Everton's 1995 FA Cup semi-final and scored twice?
sub: Joe Royle had only told him to warm up. Everton beat Tottenham.
note: Confirmed: he substituted himself into the semi-final against Tottenham while Rideout was being treated, Royle having only told him to warm up, and scored twice.

q: Which Brazilian said after signing for Manchester City in 2008 that Chelsea had made him a great offer, then corrected himself?
sub: Yeah, Manchester, sorry, he said when a reporter put him right.
note: Confirmed with the quotes: On the last day, Chelsea made a great proposal and I accepted, then You mean Manchester, right, then Yeah, Manchester, sorry. Same transfer as the Real Madrid row but a different fact, so not a mirror.

q: Which Swede had a clause in his 1999 Sunderland contract voiding it if he travelled beyond the Earth's atmosphere?
sub: He had publicly talked about becoming a space tourist.
note: Confirmed: joined Sunderland on 29 July 1999 for a club record fee and the club inserted a Space Clause making the contract wholly invalid if he travelled beyond Earth's atmosphere. The sub said he had talked about buying a ticket; his article only says he publicly expressed a desire to become a space tourist, so I pulled it back to that.

q: Which Dutch defender spent four years at Chelsea on about 40,000 pounds a week and played twelve times?
sub: Claudio Ranieri wanted him gone. He sat out the contract instead.
note: Confirmed: he appeared 12 times in a four-year tenure on a reported 40,000 pounds a week, Ranieri wanted him out weeks after he arrived, and he chose to honour the contract to the letter.
